name: Starter: Kurmanji Kurdish
about: Kurmanji word order, ezafe, cases, and verbs in useful everyday sentences.

words.ez: I (min: me, my, or a past transitive doer)
words.vexwarin: to drink (vedixwim: I drink; venaxwim: I don't drink)
words.bûn: to be, to become (present: -im, -î, -e/-ye, -in; bibim: that I become)
words.ev: this, these (oblique: vî masculine, vê feminine; van plural)
words.hebûn: to exist (heye: there is; hene: there are)
words.kirin: to do, make (dikim: I do; bikî: that you do)
words.mal: house, home (f.; mala min: my house)
words.jiyîn: to live (dijî: he or she lives)
words.çûn: to go (diçim: I go; çûn: we went; biçim: that I go)
words.rawestgeh: stop, station (f.; rawestgeha otobêsê: bus stop)
words.karîn: can, to be able (dikarî: you can)
words.ji: from, of; beginning of ji … re
words.bi: with, by, in; beginning of bi … re
words.ew: he, she, it, they, that, those (oblique: wî/wê singular; wan plural)
words.dîtin: to see (dît: saw singular; dîtin: saw plural; bibînin: that we/they see)
words.di: in; beginning of di … de or di … re
words.em: we (me: us or our in the oblique)
words.derî: door (m.; deriyê kevn: the old door)
words.vekirin: to open (veke: open; veneke: don't open)
words.kerem: grace, favor (ji kerema xwe re: please)
words.re: postposition completing bi, ji, or di
words.hatin: to come, arrive (hatim: I came; hat: it came)
words.xwarin: food, meal; to eat (dixwin: we eat; xwarin: ate them)
words.borîn: to pass; to pardon (bibore: excuse me, sorry)
words.rê: way, road (f.; vê rêyê: this way)
words.ê: will, short future marker after a pronoun

silav-tu-cawa-yi.about: Literally hello, you how are; the everyday greeting and question to one person.

ji-kerema-xwe-re.about: Literally for your grace; the standard polite phrase before or after a request.

bibore.about: Literally pardon or let it pass; used to get attention or apologize.

li-ku.about: Literally at where; used to ask where a place or thing is.

hin-bun.about: Literally to become familiar or learned: Kurmancî hîn bibim, that I learn Kurmanji.

alikari-kirin.about: Literally to do help: alîkariya min bikî, that you help me.

ser-kar.about: Literally on work; after a motion verb it means to work, and with location it means at work.

paqij-kirin.about: Literally “to do clean,” it is the usual expression for cleaning something.

concept.line: The present usually has di- plus the present stem and a person ending: diaxivî, dixwin, dimînim.
After a consonant the copula is im, î, e, or in; after a vowel it is me, yî, ye, or ne: ez baş im, tu çawa yî, ew li ku ye, em li vir in.

words.means: me = am; î = are; yî = are

concept.line: A noun takes -ê if masculine, -a if feminine, and -ên if plural before its owner or description: navê te, mala min, xwişkên min.

words.means: heye = there is; hene = there are; tune = there is none
hevalekî = a friend; hevala = female friend of

concept.line: The possessed noun takes ezafe and the owner is an oblique pronoun: mala min (my house), pirtûka te (your book), xaniyê me (our house).

words.means: nakim = do not do; dikî = do

concept.line: The usual order is subject–object–verb: Ez çay vedixwim (I drink tea).

words.means: maleke = a house; mal = house; mala = house of
diçim = go, am going; diçî = go, are going; diçe = goes

concept.line: ma may introduce a yes/no question, while çi, kî, ku, kengî, çawa, and çiqas ask for missing information: Navê te çi ye?
